## Research Complete: Terminal Visualization Guidelines

I've created a comprehensive guide at `.claude/knowledge/docs/terminal_visualization.md` covering:

### Key Findings:

**ANSI Color Support:**
- 4 levels: Basic 8-color (universal), 16-color (95%), 256-color (90%), True Color (70%)
- Windows Terminal has full support; legacy CMD/PowerShell 5 limited
- macOS Terminal.app lacks true color; iTerm2 fully supported
- Linux varies by terminal emulator

**Log Level Standards:**
- Industry follows syslog severity levels (0-7)
- Color mapping: Red (errors), Yellow (warnings), Green (info), Gray (debug)
- Color-blind safe palette using orange instead of red-green combinations

**Accessibility Requirements:**
- WCAG AA: 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum
- 8% of males have color vision deficiency
- Never rely solely on color - always include text/symbol indicators

**Emoji Best Practices:**
- Safe Unicode set: ✓✗⚡ℹ⚠●○◐→←↑↓
- Platform detection essential - provide ASCII fallbacks
- Windows Terminal supports emojis; legacy terminals need text alternatives

**Performance Optimizations:**
- Batch ANSI sequences to reduce write calls
- Cache color decisions per severity level
- Implement rate limiting for real-time streaming

The guide includes implementation checklists, testing strategies, code examples, and a cross-platform compatibility matrix.
